 From family adventures to thrillers
 What’s in cinemas this weekend
 November 6, 2026
 30
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 Moviegoers looking for something to watch this weekend have a varied lineup to choose from, with family dramas, fantasy adventures, romantic comedies, psychological thrillers and concert screenings among the latest offerings reviewed by the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB).
 With this first weekend of November underway, the agency has released classifications ranging from Parental Guidance (PG) to R-16 for nine films and concert presentations, giving audiences a guide to what may be suitable for their families.
 MTRCB Chair and CEO Lala Sotto welcomed the selection of entertainment options while reminding parents to check age classifications before heading to cinemas.
 Common caption: Filipino-produced drama ‘Buddy’ and sci-fi movie ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ both receive PG ratings. PHOTOS FROM FACEBOOK/MTRCBGOV
 For families, the Filipino-produced drama “Buddy,” starring Michael de Mesa, Benjie Paras, EA Guzman, Elijah Canlas, Elisse Joson, Empoy Marquez and Shaira Diaz, received a PG rating for its mature family themes. The film explores parental responsibility, emotional neglect, trust, forgiveness and communication within the household.

 Science-fiction fans, meanwhile, can look forward to “Godzilla Minus Zero,” featuring Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe. The latest entry in the long-running monster franchise was classified PG for its minimal, non-graphic depictions of violence and suffering.
 Common caption: Filipino-produced drama ‘Buddy’ and sci-fi movie ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ both receive PG ratings. PHOTOS FROM FACEBOOK/MTRCBGOV
 Advertisement 
 Fantasy and adventure are also represented by “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” which received a PG rating and is listed for exclusive screenings at SM Cinemas. Based on the Indian epic, the film features Ranbir Kapoor, Ravi Dubey, Sai Pallavi and Sunny Deol.
 Younger audiences also have “The Cat in the Hat,” based on the beloved Dr. Seuss children’s book and featuring the voices of Bill Hader, America Ferrera and Xochitl Gomez.
 K-pop enthusiasts have two concert screenings to consider. “Stray Kids World Tour,” scheduled for November 7 exclusively at SM Cinemas, and “EXO PLANET #6 - EXhOrizon [dot],” scheduled for November 8, both received PG classifications.
 For viewers seeking more mature stories, the South Korean psychological thriller “Paradise Lost,” starring Kim Hyun-joo, was rated R-13 for themes involving kidnapping, murder and suicide.
 Advertisement 
 Also receiving an R-13 classification is “Wicker,” a romantic comedy featuring Alexander Skarsgård, Olivia Colman and Elizabeth Debicki.
 Action fans looking for more intense fare can consider “Hellhound,” starring Louis Mandylor, Panya Yimmumphai and Vithaya Pansringarm.
